newsitem.title: USA: Dayton Hudson June same store sales rise.
newsitem.headline: Dayton Hudson June same store sales rise.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp said Thursday its same store sales for the five weeks to July 5 rose 2.9 percent from the comparable period a year ago.
Total sales in June increased 7.9 percent to $2.396 billion from $2.220 billion a year ago.

"Sales for the month of June were essentially on plan at Target and the Department Stores, and below expectations at Mervyn's," said Bob Ulrich, chairman and chief executive officer of Dayton Hudson, in a news release.
June and year-to-date sales by division were as follows:
-- Target's total sales for the month rose 13.2 percent and comparable-store sales rose 4.5 percent. Year-to-date, Target's total sales rose 13.7 percent and comparable-store sales rose 5.0 percent.
-- Mervyn's total sales for the month fell 9.0 percent and comparable-store sales fell 0.7 percent. Year-to-date, Mervyn's total sales fell 5.0 percent and comparable-store sales fell 1.0 percent.

-- The Department Store Division's total sales for the month fell 0.4 percent and comparable-store sales fell 2.4 percent. Year-to-date, the Department Stores total sales fell 0.1 percent and comparable-store sales fell 2.7 percent.

Total company sales for the 22 weeks ended July 5, 1997 were $10.02 billion, up 8.8 percent from $9.21 billion in the same period a year ago. Comparable-store sales for the 22-week period rose 3.1 percent compared with the same period last year.
Dayton Hudson operates 1,092 stores in 39 states. This includes 752 Target stores, 276 Mervyn's stores and 64 Department Stores.
